title: api: unify rate-limit semantics, idempotency keys, and retry-after across OpenAI compat layer
author: Alex Kim
description: Motivation: Inconsistencies in rate-limit responses and idempotency behavior across Redwood's native API and the OpenAI-compatibility layer were causing customer confusion and retry storms. This PR standardizes semantics and headers (Retry-After), harmonizes error codes and payload shapes for rate limits and idempotency conflicts, and adds comprehensive tests and docs. Goals: 1) Ensure clients using OpenAI-compatible endpoints receive the same rate-limit headers and 429 error semantics as Redwood native endpoints. 2) Make idempotency key handling deterministic across retries and backend failures (clear 409 vs 202 semantics). 3) Surface a consistent error JSON shape with code/message/metadata for programmatic handling. Changes include code, tests, docs, and a short compatibility shim—no change to existing default behavior for customers until feature-flag is enabled. Checklist: [x] Design doc linked (Linear ENG-2314) [x] Updated middleware in redwood/openai_compat [x] Feature-flag added (openai_compat.rate_limit_v2) [x] Unit + integration tests updated/added [x] E2E streaming + function-calling checks for Retry-After and idempotency [x] Docs and release notes updated Related: Linear ENG-2314, ENG-2478, PM-89; bug report SUP-4122. Backport: None planned; behavior gated by feature-flag to allow gradual rollout.

redwood/openai_compat/middleware/idempotency.py — deterministic state machine for idempotency keys: PENDING->COMPLETED/CONFLICT; maps to 202 (accepted) when background work scheduled, 409 when conflict with differing result; stores canonical result metadata
redwood/openai_compat/errors.py — canonical error shape: {"code": string, "message": string, "type": string, "param": optional, "metadata": optional} (compat wrapper for OpenAI shape)
